member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.close_notify
member.summary: This message notifies the recipient that the sender will not send any more messages on this connection.
member.remarks: Note that as of TLS 1.1, failure to properly close a connection no longer requires that a session not be resumed. This is a change from TLS 1.0 ("The session becomes unresumable if any connection is terminated without proper close_notify messages with level equal to warning.") to conform with widespread implementation practice.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.unexpected_message
member.summary: An inappropriate message was received.
member.remarks: This alert is always fatal and should never be observed in communication between proper implementations.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.bad_record_mac
member.summary: This alert is returned if a record is received with an incorrect MAC.
member.remarks: This alert also MUST be returned if an alert is sent because a TLSCiphertext decrypted in an invalid way: either it wasn't an even multiple of the block length, or its padding values, when checked, weren't correct. This message is always fatal and should never be observed in communication between proper implementations (except when messages were corrupted in the network).

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.decryption_failed
member.remarks: This alert was used in some earlier versions of TLS, and may have permitted certain attacks against the CBC mode [CBCATT]. It MUST NOT be sent by compliant implementations.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.record_overflow
member.summary: A TLSCiphertext record was received that had a length more than 2^14+2048 bytes, or a record decrypted to a TLSCompressed record with more than 2^14+1024 bytes.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal and should never be observed in communication between proper implementations (except when messages were corrupted in the network).

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.decompression_failure
member.summary: The decompression function received improper input (e.g., data that would expand to excessive length).
member.remarks: This message is always fatal and should never be observed in communication between proper implementations.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.handshake_failure
member.summary: Reception of a handshake_failure alert message indicates that the sender was unable to negotiate an acceptable set of security parameters given the options available.
member.remarks: This is a fatal error.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.no_certificate
member.remarks: This alert was used in SSLv3 but not any version of TLS. It MUST NOT be sent by compliant implementations.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.bad_certificate
member.summary: A certificate was corrupt, contained signatures that did not verify correctly, etc.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.unsupported_certificate
member.summary: A certificate was of an unsupported type.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.certificate_revoked
member.summary: A certificate was revoked by its signer.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.certificate_expired
member.summary: A certificate has expired or is not currently valid.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.certificate_unknown
member.summary: Some other (unspecified) issue arose in processing the certificate, rendering it unacceptable.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.illegal_parameter
member.summary: A field in the handshake was out of range or inconsistent with other fields.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.unknown_ca
member.summary: A valid certificate chain or partial chain was received, but the certificate was not accepted because the CA certificate could not be located or couldn't be matched with a known, trusted CA.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.access_denied
member.summary: A valid certificate was received, but when access control was applied, the sender decided not to proceed with negotiation.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.decode_error
member.summary: A message could not be decoded because some field was out of the specified range or the length of the message was incorrect.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal and should never be observed in communication between proper implementations (except when messages were corrupted in the network).

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.decrypt_error
member.summary: A handshake cryptographic operation failed, including being unable to correctly verify a signature or validate a Finished message.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.export_restriction
member.remarks: This alert was used in some earlier versions of TLS. It MUST NOT be sent by compliant implementations.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.protocol_version
member.summary: The protocol version the client has attempted to negotiate is recognized but not supported.
member.remarks: (For example, old protocol versions might be avoided for security reasons.) This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.insufficient_security
member.summary: Returned instead of handshake_failure when a negotiation has failed specifically because the server requires ciphers more secure than those supported by the client.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.internal_error
member.summary: An internal error unrelated to the peer or the correctness of the protocol (such as a memory allocation failure) makes it impossible to continue.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.user_canceled
member.summary: This handshake is being canceled for some reason unrelated to a protocol failure.
member.remarks: If the user cancels an operation after the handshake is complete, just closing the connection by sending a close_notify is more appropriate. This alert should be followed by a close_notify. This message is generally a warning.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.no_renegotiation
member.summary: Sent by the client in response to a hello request or by the server in response to a client hello after initial handshaking.
member.remarks: Either of these would normally lead to renegotiation; when that is not appropriate, the recipient should respond with this alert. At that point, the original requester can decide whether to proceed with the connection. One case where this would be appropriate is where a server has spawned a process to satisfy a request; the process might receive security parameters (key length, authentication, etc.) at startup, and it might be difficult to communicate changes to these parameters after that point. This message is always a warning.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.unsupported_extension
member.summary: Sent by clients that receive an extended server hello containing an extension that they did not put in the corresponding client hello.
member.remarks: This message is always fatal.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Tls.AlertDescription.certificate_unobtainable
member.summary: This alert is sent by servers who are unable to retrieve a certificate chain from the URL supplied by the client(see Section 3.3).
member.remarks: This message MAY be fatal - for example if client authentication is required by the server for the handshake to continue and the server is unable to retrieve the certificate chain, it may send a fatal alert.

If any records containing application data were processed, the decrypted data can be obtained using . If any records containing protocol data were processed, a response may have been generated. You should always check to see if there is any available output after calling this method by calling .

Validate the time stamp token.
To be valid the token must be signed by the passed in certificate and the certificate must be the one referred to by the SigningCertificate attribute included in the hashed attributes of the token. A successful call to validate means all the above are true.

Convert binary data to and from UrlBase64 encoding. This is identical to Base64 encoding, except that the padding character is "." and the other non-alphanumeric characters are "-" and "_" instead of "+" and "/".
The purpose of UrlBase64 encoding is to provide a compact encoding of binary data that is safe for use as an URL parameter. Base64 encoding does not produce encoded values that are safe for use in URLs, since "/" can be interpreted as a path delimiter; "+" is the encoded form of a space; and "=" is used to separate a name from the corresponding value in an URL parameter.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.CmsAllowLenientRsaPkcs1
member.summary: Allow legacy RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 key-transport unwrap in CMS when the content-encryption key has no fixed size.
member.remarks: Without a fixed key size to target, the standard constant-time defense against the Bleichenbacher padding Oracle cannot be applied. Setting this property to 'true' allows the unwrap to proceed anyway, which is not recommended, since it leaves the padding oracle intact.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.PbeMaxIterationCount
member.summary: Upper bound on the PBKDF2 iteration count honoured when decrypting a PBES2-protected PKCS#8/PEM private key.
member.remarks: The key-derivation parameters travel inside the (unauthenticated) encrypted-key container, so an unbounded count makes decrypting attacker-supplied key material a CPU-exhaustion vector. Default 5,000,000.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.PbeMaxScryptMemory
member.summary: Upper bound, in bytes, on the scrypt working memory (~128 * N * r) honoured when decrypting a PBES2-protected PKCS#8 / PEM private key.
member.remarks: As with the scrypt cost travels in the unauthenticated container, so an unbounded cost is a memory-exhaustion vector. Default 1073741824 (1 GiB).

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.Pkcs12IgnoreUselessPassword
member.summary: When set to true, suppresses the error raised when loading a PKCS12 store with a password, for data that does not require a password.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.Pkcs12MaxIterationCount
member.summary: If set, a PKCS12 file with a larger iteration count on PBE processing will be rejected. Default 5,000,000.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.PKMacMaxIterationCount
member.summary: Upper bound on the RFC 4211 PKMAC / CMP password-based-MAC iteration count honoured when no explicit ceiling is supplied.
member.remarks: The count travels in the (unauthenticated) PBMParameter of an incoming CMP message and drives an iterated hash, so an unbounded count makes verifying an attacker-supplied message a CPU-exhaustion vector. Default 1,000,000.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.X509Sgp22NameConstraints
member.summary: Opt in to the relaxed directoryName name-constraint matching required by GSMA SGP.22 v2.5 (Remote SIM Provisioning), sections 4.5.2.1.0.2 / 4.5.2.1.0.3. When set, a permitted-subtree RDN is satisfied by any matching subject RDN regardless of position, additional subject attributes beyond those named in the subtree are tolerated, and a serialNumber RDN is matched with a StartsWith comparison wherever it appears. This is deliberately looser than the contiguous-prefix DN matching mandated by RFC 5280 7.1, so it defaults to off and must be enabled explicitly; BC's default validation remains RFC 5280 strict.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.X509AllowLenientRfc822Name
member.summary: Fall back to the legacy lenient parsing of rfc822Name values in X.509 name-constraint checks. By default the validator is strict about rfc822Name conformance; today that means a tested rfc822Name with more than one '@' is rejected as ambiguous when email constraints apply (RFC 5321 sec. 4.1.2 allows '@' inside a quoted local part, so the domain is not simply the text after the first '@', and a wrong split could evade a constraint). When set, that strictness (and any future rfc822Name conformance strictness) is disabled and the historical permissive parsing is used instead. Strict is the default; set this only to restore the old behaviour. This is a safety valve, not a recommended mode.

member.name: F:Org.BouncyCastle.Utilities.Properties.X509AllowLenientIPAddressMask
member.summary: Salvage a non-contiguous iPAddress name-constraint subnet mask instead of rejecting it. An iPAddress name constraint carries a subnet mask expected to be CIDR (a run of leading 1-bits); a non-contiguous mask is malformed per RFC 4632 and also lets the subtree set-algebra mint new ranges (a super-linear blow-up on hostile input). By default such a constraint is rejected (fail-closed). When set, the mask is instead rounded to the most-restrictive contiguous mask for its context - a permitted subtree is narrowed (fill up to the last 1-bit; under-permit), an excluded subtree is broadened (keep only the leading 1-bits; over-exclude) - so validation can only get stricter, never laxer. Strict rejection is the default; this is a safety valve, not a recommended mode.

Holder ::= SEQUENCE { baseCertificateID [0] IssuerSerial OPTIONAL, -- the issuer and serial number of -- the holder's Public Key Certificate entityName [1] GeneralNames OPTIONAL, -- the name of the claimant or role objectDigestInfo [2] ObjectDigestInfo OPTIONAL -- used to directly authenticate the holder, -- for example, an executable }

members.member:
Constructs a holder for v2 attribute certificates with a hash value for some type of object.
digestedObjectType can be one of the following:
0 - publicKey - A hash of the public key of the holder must be passed.
1 - publicKeyCert - A hash of the public key certificate of the holder must be passed.
2 - otherObjectDigest - A hash of some other object type must be passed. otherObjectTypeID must not be empty.
This cannot be used if a v1 attribute certificate is used.
@param digestedObjectType The digest object type. @param digestAlgorithm The algorithm identifier for the hash. @param otherObjectTypeID The object type ID if digestedObjectType is otherObjectDigest. @param objectDigest The hash value.
